newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Gorbachev tells Rio +5 of need to change our ways.
newsitem.headline: Gorbachev tells Rio +5 of need to change our ways.

text.p: Former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev, speaking at the Rio +5 environmental meeting on Monday, said "civil society" was the key to solving the world's environmental problems.
Rio +5 brings together hundreds of environmentalists, business leaders and U.N. officials for a week to review and revive pledges made at the 1992 Earth Summit.

"Things will only change very slowly unless civil society speaks up. Civil society is the most important factor in changing policies, in changing everything," said Gorbachev, who is attending the meeting as president of the environmental group Green Cross International.
He said people had to reassess their way of life, limit their consumption and learn to be more modest before human intervention in nature brought about irreversible damage to the biosphere.
Conference organisers and participants agree that governments have done little to resolve issues that are as pressing now as they were during the Earth Summit in 1992.
They say there has been more progress by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the business sector to promote sustainable development than on the part of governments.
Gorbachev said now that the antagonism of the Cold War was over, countries should sit down together and draw on the best ideas from different ideologies to find solutions.

"I disagree with the approach that any one single ideological stance could be a sort of panacea for the resolution of all the problems," he said. "To construct the new building of the new world we need many different values, socialist values, liberal values, conservative values."

He said that with greater globalization, the United Nations had an important role to play. Even though its institutions should be reformed, everything possible should be done to give the U.N. a second wind, he said.
"We have to sit down together so the world in the future will not suffer the hegemony of one country," Gorbachev said. "The world should be one of unity and diversity."

Gorbachev is the European representative on a panel drawing up a draft Earth Charter that is being presented to heads of state when they meet at the United Nations in New York in June to carry out their own reappraisal of the Earth Summit.

Unlike the 1992 conference, Rio +5 is a purely non-governmental gathering with no heads of state or government representatives attending, which means there will be no grand resolutions or declarations. The conference ends on Wednesday.
